title: Do Language Models Know Which Words Steer Their Reasoning?
abstract: arXiv:2611.27317v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits intermediate reasoning steps from language models, it is unclear which words in the context actually steer the CoT. We identify Phantom Context Influence (PCI): language models are disproportionately steered by semantically irrelevant context words, even as the same models deny those words' relevance when asked. To localize PCI, we introduce Leave-One-Out Word JSD analysis, which removes one context word at a time from the otherwise intact context to isolate its marginal effect on the next-token distribution; words whose removal flips the prediction (pivot words) are passed to the same LLM to self-judge whether it recognizes this predictive dependence. Across four models and three benchmarks, language models largely do not know which words steer their reasoning, a mismatch we call the Generation-Judgment Contradiction. Inspired by this phenomenon, we propose Online KV Suppression: it score

translated_title: 语言模型知道自己推理被哪些词引导吗？
translated_abstract: 虽然思维链提示能够引导语言模型产生中间推理步骤，但目前尚不清楚上下文中哪些词真正引导了思维链。我们识别出了“幻影上下文影响”现象：语言模型会被语义无关的上下文词不成比例地引导，即使同一模型在被直接询问时会否认这些词的相关性。为了定位这一现象，我们引入了“留一词JSD分析”，该方法从原本完整的上下文中每次移除一个词，以隔离该词对下一个词元分布的边际影响；移除后会导致预测翻转的词（枢轴词）会被传递给同一个大语言模型，让其自我判断是否识别到这种预测依赖关系。在四个模型和三个基准上的实验表明，语言模型在很大程度上并不知道哪些词引导了它们的推理，我们将这种不匹配称为“生成-判断矛盾”。受此现象启发，我们提出了“在线KV抑制”方法……
tldr: 该论文发现了“幻影上下文影响”现象——语言模型的推理会被语义无关的词不成比例地引导，而模型自身却意识不到这种依赖关系（生成-判断矛盾），并提出“在线KV抑制”方法来缓解这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies Phantom Context Influence (PCI)—language models are disproportionately steered by semantically irrelevant context words while denying their relevance, a mismatch termed the Generation-Judgment Contradiction—and proposes Online KV Suppression to address it.
